item.title: 'Free tickets + $50 for Melania movie': Craigslist Ad offers money for documentary, says 'must remain in seats for entire film'
item.description: Despite claims of a fast sell-out, a new documentary about Melania Trump's private life reportedly saw nearly empty theaters on opening night in Boston. An advertisement offering free tickets and $50 to attendees in Boston went viral, highlighting sluggish ticket sales nationwide and internationally.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Who is Jennifer O’Brien? TikTok influencer jailed for 17 years after court confirms at least 10 serious crimes
item.description: TikTok creator Jennifer O’Brien, known online as Jennifer Nieve, has been jailed for 17 years after a Manchester court found she physically abused a woman at least 10 times. The judge called the crimes repeated and deeply harmful. The victim described long-term fear and anxiety. The case was reported by the Manchester Evening News.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: Inside Candace Owens’ bond with Charlie Kirk: From best friends to Erika Kirk controversy after his death
item.description: Candace Owens and Charlie Kirk shared a close friendship that began in 2017 and lasted until Kirk’s death in 2025. After his passing, Owens spoke openly about her grief and later clashed with Kirk’s wife, Erika Kirk. The situation grew more tense after Owens shared a leaked audio, according to Us Weekly.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: TikTok star and activist Shirley Raines of Beauty 2 the Streetz dies at 58
item.description: Shirley Raines, known as Ms. Shirley and founder of Beauty 2 the Streetz, has died at 58. She gained popularity on TikTok for her work providing beauty and hygiene services to unhoused communities in Los Angeles and Nevada. Her passing was confirmed by her organization, which highlighted her tireless advocacy and the lasting impact she made.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: Twitch streamer Duke Dennis says streaming beats 9-to-5 jobs after claiming huge earnings
item.description: Popular streamer Duke Dennis sparked debate by stating streaming surpasses 9-to-5 jobs. He claimed a $500k stream, though verified earnings show a different picture. His comments highlight streamer culture's tendency to hype earnings. While some celebrate his success, others question the claims, pointing to the disconnect from everyday work realities. Steady streaming income requires significant effort.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: BBQ fork, pizza cutter and driver’s licence: Minnesota man allegedly poses as FBI agent to free Luigi Mangione; arrested
item.description: A bizarre attempt to free a high-profile inmate at a Brooklyn jail was thwarted when a Minnesota man, armed with a BBQ fork and pizza cutter, allegedly posed as an FBI agent. He presented fake court orders to release Luigi Mangione, accused in a CEO's murder. Authorities apprehended the suspect, ensuring no inmate escape and facility operations remained undisturbed.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Helicopter crashes into Meramec River at Missouri state park; all passengers escape with 'minor injuries'
item.description: A private helicopter crashed into the Meramec River at Meramec State Park on Thursday afternoon, prompting a rescue operation for its four occupants. Trained swimmers and EMS crews were deployed to the scene, where officials confirmed the incident. The cause of the crash is under investigation, with speculation it may have involved power lines.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Watch: Trump’s ‘very famous’ Ozempic friend sparks guessing game, JD Vance says 'not me'
item.description: President Trump sparked amusement by recounting a story of a "very famous" friend for whom Ozempic didn't work. Vice President JD Vance humorously ruled himself out, leading to a lighthearted exchange that briefly overshadowed policy discussions. Trump then pivoted to discussing drug price negotiations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Senate blocks government funding package as DHS dispute stalls talks — will US face a second shutdown?
item.description: Senate Democrats and some Republicans blocked a government funding package, jeopardizing a Friday deadline and signaling ongoing negotiations. Democrats opposed the bill due to Homeland Security funding, demanding reforms to ICE's immigration crackdown. A shutdown could impact agencies like the IRS and court operations, though many departments are already funded.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Heartbroken, alone': ICE arrests 58-year-old McDonald's worker, 'laughed' at son bringing medicine for father
item.description: ICE agents allegedly mocked a teenager delivering life-saving medication to his ailing father at a detention center. The father, arrested at McDonald's, suffers from heart failure. The incident highlights concerns about ICE detention practices, with data suggesting many detainees lack criminal convictions. Public figures are voicing strong opposition to the administration's immigration policies.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Elon and Jeff best watch their backs’: British man built a £288 million fake medicine empire after winning a £2.4 million lottery
item.description: A £2.4 million lottery winner, John Spiby, transformed his windfall into a massive counterfeit medicine empire. His operation, spanning multiple sites, produced fake prescription pills estimated to be worth £288 million. Spiby's delusion was evident in his boast that tech titans should 'watch their backs'. The judge condemned his disregard for public safety.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Aspen Kartier twitch ban explained after disturbing clip goes viral
item.description: Twitch streamer Aspen Kartier has been banned from the platform following a viral video that captured concerning audio of her dog yelping repeatedly. Viewers interpreted the sounds as evidence of animal cruelty, leading to widespread backlash. The ban occurred after the disturbing clip circulated online, impacting her burgeoning content creation career.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: 'You don’t belong in this country': Police kick, use racist slurs against Muslim women in Netherlands
item.description: Two Muslim women in Utrecht, Netherlands, have filed a formal complaint after a police officer was filmed kicking and hitting them. The women's lawyer stated the officer also used racist language. Police are investigating the incident, acknowledging the video's impact and questions about racism.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Devastated UK family watches 5-year-old dying from rare childhood dementia; hundreds of seizures daily
item.description: Five-year-old Holly Nayler from Essex has CLN2 Batten disease, a rare and fatal form of childhood dementia that causes rapid neurological decline and frequent seizures. While an NHS-funded treatment cannot cure the condition, it has slowed the loss of her abilities. As access to the drug faces uncertainty, her family is calling for awareness and continued support.
item.dc:creator: TOI Trending Desk

item.title: Random Musing: A brief history of the Church of England (as it gets its first woman Archbishop of Canterbury)
item.description: It begins, inevitably, with Henry VIII, who married Catherine but couldn’t produce a male heir. The Pope refused to annul the marriage because Catherine was the aunt of Charles V, the Holy Roman Emperor whose armies effectively controlled Rome — a man at whose snook the Pope could ill afford to cock. So, Henry decided it was time to do a Thanos and take matters into his own hands.
item.dc:creator: Nirmalya Dutta

item.title: Aircraft carrier & destroyers: Decoding the firepower of Trump's 'beautiful armada' closing in on Iran
item.description: Tensions between the United States and Iran are escalating. US President Donald Trump has warned Iran to negotiate a nuclear deal or face severe military action. A large US naval fleet, including an aircraft carrier and destroyers, is moving into West Asia. This deployment raises fears of an imminent military confrontation.
